source_row.stem: A nurse counsels a pregnant client taking an SSRI about potential effects on the newborn, and the client assumes any risk mentioned would automatically mean every exposed newborn ends up needing NICU care. The nurse should instead mention:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"SSRIs are considered absolutely contraindicated in every single pregnancy, rather than a decision requiring individualized risk-benefit discussion with the provider as is actually the case","B":"Poor neonatal adaptation syndrome, with transient jitteriness or breathing difficulty possible in newborns exposed late in pregnancy","C":"There is no possible effect on the newborn whatsoever, despite documented cases of transient neonatal symptoms following late-pregnancy exposure to this medication class","D":"NICU admission is certain in every exposed newborn, rather than only in the smaller subset who go on to develop noticeable symptoms as the client is currently assuming"}}
source_row.rationale: SSRI exposure late in pregnancy can be associated with poor neonatal adaptation syndrome in some newborns, with transient symptoms such as jitteriness, feeding difficulty, or respiratory distress, requiring monitoring after birth.
source_row.source_name: FDA Prescribing Information — SSRIs, Pregnancy Considerations
